controlled_change: Immediate versus coalesced submissions, with identical 1072-slot CLOCK cache, 12GiB maximum, eight readers and two alternating request pairs.
correctness: All requested tokens and arithmetic dispatch counts match; native eviction, cancellation, read-failure and ownership tests passed.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: Remove driver scheduling overhead while preserving exact experts and arithmetic.
hypothesis: Collecting remaining single-token expert reads into one command group reduces request latency by at least 20ms per token.
limitations: Single M1 Pro, short 72-token initial request and 128-token retained append; no 2K/4K/7K or sustained-coding acceptance.
Production defaults remain unchanged. Paired intervals assume approximately independent log ratios; temporal host effects can violate this.
outcome: Every process was clean. Submissions fell from about 330-349 to 144-145 per token, but decode became 5.9% slower initially and 8.9% slower after append. Conversation latency increased about 2.6%.
smallest_experiment: Keep immediate expert execution; do not infer request benefit from fewer command groups alone.
